name: Saddle sUSD metapool stale MetaSwapUtils library

classification.summary: The sUSDv2 MetaSwap pool was linked against an outdated MetaSwapUtils library whose swapUnderlying() priced the base-pool LP token from raw pool balances instead of its virtual price, so flash-loan-driven sUSD/saddleUSD-V2 swaps repeatedly bought the LP token below value and drained the metapool.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

limitations: Target identity and code history came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/saddle-finance.json; no semantic revalidation was inherited.
The executing code artifact and its code hash have not been established in structured evidence.
One or more target block, transaction, ordering, or creator anchors remain unresolved.

sources.note: onchain review: metapool 0x824dcd7b044d60df2e89b1bb888e66d8bcf41491 created 2021-12-15 by 0x5bdb37d0ddea3a90f233c7b7f6b9394b6b2eef34 (Saddle deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0x63341ba917de90498f3903b199df5699b4a55ac0; attack tx located from the pool's own logs at block 14684307; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events - the flawed library link was fixed at deployment time and never changed, so age = deployment; Saddle's post-mortem states $11.9M drained of which $3.97M was front-run and returned by BlockSec

re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis. The metapool's runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 13806669 and the incident block 14684307, and its 11 DELEGATECALL sites are solc external-library calls to three link-time-hardcoded addresses - 0x2069043d7556b1207a505eb459d18d908df29b55, 0x3661d0f70e7f3ec418321a57fd62d691a09b490b and 0x88cc4aa0dd6cf126b00c012dda9f6f4fd9388b17 - each of whose runtimes begins 73<self>3014 and is constant across the window. callTracer on the exploit tx shows the pool delegatecalling only 0x88cc4aa0..., i.e. the stale MetaSwapUtils this row names, so the link is fixed at deploy time and the deployment basis is exact.
